cases.title: Every cluster better by 1/2: pass
cases.derivation: d_c = 1 - 1/2 = 1/2 for k=6. Two-sided p: only the all-plus and all-minus assignments reach |sum| = 3, so 2/64 = 1/32. r = floor(0.025*64) = 1, so L = smallest subset mean = 1/2 and U = 1/2. L > -0.05: pass.

cases.title: Zero difference: non-inferior, pass
cases.derivation: All d_c = 0, so every assignment gives |sum| = 0 >= 0 and p = 64/64 = 1. L = U = 0 > -0.05: pass. Non-inferiority means 'not worse by more than the margin'.

cases.title: Bound exactly at -margin: inconclusive (strict inequalities)
cases.derivation: margin = 1/2 and d_c = -1/2. L = -1/2 is not > -1/2, and U = -1/2 is not < -1/2: inconclusive.

cases.title: Five clusters cannot be decisive
cases.derivation: k=5: r = floor(0.025*32) = 0, so there is no finite bound and the outcome is inconclusive. Two-sided p = 2/32 = 1/16, which can't fall below 0.05 with 5 clusters.

cases.title: Distinct differences, k=7: order statistics
cases.derivation: d = 1/10..7/10. r = floor(0.025*128) = 3. Sorted subset means start 1/10 ({1}), 3/20 ({1,2}), then 1/5 ({2} and {1,3}), so L = 1/5. From the top: 7/10, 13/20, 3/5, so U = 3/5. Flipping the smallest term already drops the sum below 28/10, so p = 2/128 = 1/64. L > -0.05: pass.

cases.title: Mixed signs: inconclusive
cases.derivation: d = [1, 1, 1, -1, -1, 0]. L = smallest subset mean = -1, U = 1; the interval spans -0.05. The five non-zero terms are ±1, so every assignment's sum is odd, |sum| >= 1 = observed, and p = 1.

cases.title: Unadjudicated findings: a provisional pass cannot pass
cases.derivation: Same as D-01 plus 1 unresolved finding. Adjudication could change either yield, so the outcome is inconclusive and the provisional outcome is recorded as pass.

cases.title: Undefined yield counts as 0 under the default policy
cases.derivation: Cluster 6 has B submitted 0, so b = 0 and d_6 = -1/2. The other five d = 1/2. L = -1/2 spans the margin: inconclusive. mean = (5/2 - 1/2)/6 = 1/3. Two-sided p: every assignment is six ±1/2 terms; |sum| >= 2 when at least five share a sign: C(6,0)+C(6,1)+C(6,5)+C(6,6) = 14, so 14/64 = 7/32.

cases.title: Undefined yield excluded under exclude_cluster: too few clusters
cases.derivation: Cluster 6 is excluded, leaving k=5 (no finite bound): inconclusive. p = 2/32 = 1/16.

cases.title: Vacuous pass: the baseline confirmed nothing, so no candidate could fail; inconclusive
cases.derivation: A submits 3 findings per cluster and none is confirmed (yield 0); B submits nothing (undefined, 0 under the default policy). All d_c = 0, so p = 64/64 = 1 and L = U = 0 > -0.05: a provisional pass. Worst case for B (yield 0 in every cluster): d_c = -0 = 0, L = 0 > -0.05, so a pass was certain whatever B did. Outcome inconclusive.

cases.title: Vacuous pass: both configurations silent everywhere, as a broken runner or grader would be
cases.derivation: Every cluster is 0/0 on both sides, so both yields are 0 under the default policy and all d_c = 0: p = 1, L = U = 0, a provisional pass. The worst case for B is the same data, L = 0 > -0.05: vacuous, inconclusive.

cases.title: Vacuous pass: baseline yield below the margin in every cluster, even with a better B
cases.derivation: A = 1/25 and B = 1/5 in every cluster, so d_c = 4/25, p = 2/64 = 1/32, L = U = 4/25 > -0.05: a provisional pass. Worst case for B: d_c = -1/25, L = -1/25 > -1/20, so no B could fail. Inconclusive; to claim that B beats a weak baseline, pre-register margin 0 (D-14).

cases.title: Weak baseline with margin 0: the superiority pass is informative, not vacuous
cases.derivation: The D-13 data under margin 0. L = 4/25 > 0: pass. Worst case for B: L = -1/25, which is not > 0, so a B with yield 0 would not have passed. The pass stands.

cases.title: Mostly silent baseline: one measurable cluster makes the pass informative
cases.derivation: A = 0/2 in five clusters and 1/2 in c6; B equals A. All d_c = 0: p = 1, L = U = 0 > -0.05, pass. Worst case for B: d = (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, -1/2); r = 1, so L = the smallest subset mean = -1/2 < -0.05: a B with yield 0 would not have passed. The pass stands; the rule is exact, not 'A is zero somewhere'.

optional-adjudication.description: Complete adjudication is required in v0.1.

other-metric.description: The primary metric is fixed by ADR-0006.

alpha-too-large.description: alpha is per side and below 0.5.

too-many-clusters.description: The exact gate enumerates 2^k sign assignments: a cohort names at most 20 clusters.

clustered_wilson.derivation: No cluster has a trial: no interval (None), as for wilson with 0 trials.
Only one cluster has trials. One independent unit cannot bound a proportion: t with 0 degrees of freedom is unbounded, and the score interval tends to [0, 1].

The M2 live slice shape: R = 3/12 = 1/4, every residual c - R n = 1 - 1 = 0, so V = 0 and the effective n is N = 12 (Korn-Graubard convention). k = 3 gives t(0.975, 2) = 0.95 * sqrt(2 / 0.0975) = 4.30265. Wilson(1/4, 12, 4.30265) = [0.031860, 0.771502]; the naive interval with z = 1.95996 is [0.088942, 0.532305].

Clusters agree more than independent trials would: R = 22/40 = 0.55, residuals +-1/2, V = (4/3) * 1 / 1600 = 1/1200, R (1 - R) / V = 297 > N = 40, so the effective n is capped at 40. Only the quantile changes: t(0.975, 3) = 3.182446. Wilson(0.55, 40, 3.182446) = [0.316051, 0.763745].
Nothing confirmed: R = 0, V = 0, effective n = N = 18, t(0.975, 5) = 2.570582. The lower bound is 0 and the upper is t^2 / (N + t^2) = 6.607891 / 24.607891 = 0.268527.

guardrail_cases.title: Withholding: B reports only its surest finding; yield passes, the recall guardrail fails
guardrail_cases.derivation: Each cluster has 3 labeled defects. A submits 4 findings, 3 confirmed (yield 3/4, recall 3/3); B submits 1, confirmed (yield 1/1, recall 1/3). Yield: d_c = 1/4, L = U = 1/4 > -0.05, pass. Recall: d_c = 1/3 - 1 = -2/3, k = 6, r = 1, so L = U = -2/3 < -0.1: fail. Any fail is a fail.

guardrail_cases.title: Selective silence under exclude_cluster: B's empty clusters leave the yield test, not the recall test
guardrail_cases.derivation: Six clusters where A and B agree (yield 1/2, recall 1/1 each) and four where A is perfect (yield 1/1, recall 1/1) and B submits nothing (undefined yield, recall 0/1). exclude_cluster drops the four from the yield test: six d_c = 0, L = U = 0 > -0.05, pass. Recall is defined in all ten: six 0s and four -1s, k = 10, r = floor(0.025*1024) = 25. The 15 subsets of -1s alone have mean -1, the 6 subsets {four -1s, one 0} have -4/5, the next 24 ({three -1s, one 0}) have -3/4, so L = -3/4; 63 all-zero subsets give U = 0. [-3/4, 0] spans -0.1: inconclusive, so no pass.

guardrail_cases.title: B as good as A on both metrics: pass
guardrail_cases.derivation: Yield 1/2 and recall 1/1 on both sides in six clusters. Both tests: all d_c = 0, L = U = 0, above -0.05 and -0.1: pass.

guardrail_cases.title: A recall fail is final even while findings are unadjudicated
guardrail_cases.derivation: The G-01 rows with one unresolved finding on A in c1. The yield pass is only provisional (rule 4), but recall counts defects the matcher credited, which adjudication does not change, so the guardrail fail stands: outcome and provisional outcome are fail.
